what_this_is: Regression expectations. Each entry records what paneldx reports today on the documented key of a public panel, so that an unintended change in behaviour fails a test instead of passing unnoticed.
what_this_is_not: Scientific truth. An entry saying `inconclusive` does not mean the key is wrong or right; it means the data did not decide. Where paneldx and the documented key disagree, the documented key is the one supported by evidence (see validation/manifests/datasets.json) and the paneldx status is the thing under suspicion. No accuracy rate is claimed from these numbers; the panels listed here are development data.
how_to_change_this_file: Only alongside a deliberate, reviewed change in behaviour, with the reason recorded in CHANGELOG.md. Editing an expectation to make a red test go green is how a regression becomes a feature.

grunfeld.note: 10 firms, below the 20-entity minimum, so no verdict is issued. Many classic econometrics panels are this small.

emplUK.note: Only `sector` is invariant within a firm, 1 of 5 usable columns, which scores between the weak and supported thresholds.

produc.note: Was `fail` under 0.4.0 and is the false rejection 0.5.0 was written to remove. Only `region` is invariant within a state, 1 of 9 usable columns, which is below the weak threshold. Under 0.5.0 a low evidence share is an absence of evidence rather than evidence against, so the verdict is `inconclusive`. It is deliberately not forced to `pass`: nothing in the panel supports the key either.

gasoline.note: 18 countries, below the 20-entity minimum, so no verdict is issued.

baseline_comparison: validation/results/development/v0.4.0/ holds the same benchmark run under 0.4.0. The only development-panel verdict that changed is produc, fail -> inconclusive.
